subject: Environment
sub_topic: Levels of biodiversity — genetic, species, ecosystem

concepts.name: Genetic Diversity: Definition, Scope, and Measurement
key_dimensions: Distinction between genetic diversity within a species vs. between species (UPSC trap: confusing with species diversity)
Metrics: allelic richness, heterozygosity, gene flow — and why low heterozygosity signals conservation risk
Role of mutation, recombination, and natural selection in maintaining genetic diversity
Genetic erosion in crop wild relatives and domestic breeds — link to food security (FAO reports)

concepts.name: Species Diversity: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma Diversity
key_dimensions: Precise definitions: alpha (local/within-habitat), beta (between habitats/turnover), gamma (landscape-level) — UPSC frequently tests alpha vs. beta confusion
Indices: Shannon-Wiener, Simpson's Index — what they measure and their limitations
Relationship between species richness and species evenness — why a high-richness ecosystem can still be 'less diverse'
Application: why beta diversity is critical for designing wildlife corridors and protected area networks

concepts.name: Ecosystem Diversity: Types, Components, and Measurement Challenges
key_dimensions: Distinction between ecosystem diversity and biome diversity — UPSC trap: treating them as interchangeable
Components: diversity of habitats, communities, and ecological processes within a landscape
Why ecosystem diversity is the hardest level to quantify (no universally accepted metric unlike species richness)
India-specific context: diversity from cold deserts (Ladakh) to mangroves to shola forests — implications for policy

concepts.name: Interrelationship Among Three Levels of Biodiversity
key_dimensions: Hierarchical dependency: genetic diversity underpins species diversity, which structures ecosystem diversity
Cascade effects: loss of genetic diversity → inbreeding depression → local extinction → ecosystem restructuring
Why conservation strategies must target all three levels simultaneously (CBD mandate)
UPSC trap: assuming species-level conservation alone is sufficient — counterexamples like monoculture forests

concepts.name: Genetic Diversity and its Role in Species Resilience and Adaptation
key_dimensions: Evolutionary significance: genetic diversity as raw material for natural selection under changing environments
Minimum Viable Population (MVP) concept — why small populations lose adaptive potential
Case studies: Cheetah (extremely low genetic diversity) vs. African elephant populations
Climate change angle: species with higher genetic diversity better equipped to adapt — policy implication for assisted gene flow

concepts.name: Species Richness Patterns: Latitudinal and Altitudinal Gradients
key_dimensions: Latitudinal gradient: higher species richness near tropics — hypotheses (energy-stability, evolutionary time, productivity)
Altitudinal gradient: mid-domain effect and hump-shaped richness pattern — distinction from latitudinal gradient
UPSC trap: assuming richness always decreases monotonically with altitude (mid-elevation peak is the exception)
India's Western Ghats and Eastern Himalayas as examples of both gradients intersecting

concepts.name: Keystone Species and Their Role in Maintaining Ecosystem Diversity
key_dimensions: Definition: disproportionate impact on ecosystem structure relative to biomass — distinguish from dominant species (UPSC trap)
Examples: Sea otters, tigers as apex predators, fig trees as keystone mutualists, elephants as ecosystem engineers
Trophic cascade mechanism: how removal of keystone species collapses ecosystem diversity
Policy relevance: why keystone species identification is critical for Project Tiger, Project Elephant

concepts.name: Biodiversity Hotspots: Criteria, India's Hotspots, and Conservation Implications
key_dimensions: Norman Myers' criteria: ≥1,500 endemic vascular plant species AND ≥70% habitat loss — both conditions mandatory (UPSC 'only' clause trap)
India's four hotspots: Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Sundaland — precise geographic boundaries frequently tested
Hotspot concept limitations: focuses on endemism, may neglect species-rich but non-endemic areas like Gangetic plains
Overlap between hotspots and megadiverse countries — India is both (UPSC comparison trap)

concepts.name: Endemic Species: Definition, Distribution, and Conservation Significance
key_dimensions: Distinction: endemic (restricted range) vs. rare (low abundance) vs. endangered (threatened) — UPSC frequently conflates these
Neo-endemics vs. paleo-endemics — significance for understanding evolutionary history of a region
India's endemic richness: Western Ghats (lion-tailed macaque, purple frog), Andaman & Nicobar Islands
Why endemism makes species more vulnerable to habitat loss — direct link to IUCN Red List criteria

concepts.name: IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria: Application to Species Diversity Assessment
key_dimensions: Nine categories: Extinct, Extinct in Wild, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened, Least Concern, Data Deficient, Not Evaluated — UPSC tests precise thresholds
Five criteria (A–E): population reduction, restricted range, small population size, quantitative analysis, viability — distinction between criteria frequently tested
UPSC trap: 'Critically Endangered' is not the same as 'functionally extinct' — Great Indian Bustard example
India-specific: species that changed categories recently — cheetah (Extinct in Wild in India), gharial status

concepts.name: In-situ vs. Ex-situ Conservation: Mechanisms, Institutions, and Limitations
key_dimensions: In-situ: Protected Areas (National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves, Conservation Reserves, Community Reserves) — legal distinctions under Wildlife Protection Act 1972
Ex-situ: Seed banks, gene banks, zoological parks, botanical gardens, cryopreservation — National Gene Bank (NBPGR) role
UPSC trap: Biosphere Reserves are not under WPA 1972 (they are under UNESCO MAB Programme) — different legal basis
Complementarity argument: why ex-situ alone cannot replace in-situ (no evolutionary adaptation possible in ex-situ)

concepts.name: Genetic Erosion in Agriculture: Crop Diversity, Landraces, and the Green Revolution Trade-off
key_dimensions: Mechanism: replacement of diverse landraces with High Yielding Varieties (HYVs) → narrowing of agricultural gene pool
Vavilov Centers of Origin — India as a center for rice, mango, turmeric diversity — relevance of crop wild relatives
International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA) — distinct from CBD (UPSC trap)
National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR) and National Gene Bank — India's institutional response

concepts.name: Ecosystem Services and Their Link to Biodiversity Levels
key_dimensions: MEA framework: provisioning, regulating, cultural, supporting services — which level of biodiversity primarily sustains each
Biodiversity-ecosystem function relationship: higher diversity → greater functional redundancy → more stable service delivery
UPSC trap: ecosystem services are a subset of nature's contributions — NCP framework of IPBES is broader
Economic valuation methods: TEEB initiative, India's National Mission for Green India — policy linkage

concepts.name: Threats to Biodiversity at Each Level: HIPPO Framework
key_dimensions: HIPPO: Habitat loss, Invasive species, Pollution, Population (human), Over-exploitation — rank order of threats (habitat loss is #1 globally)
Level-specific threats: genetic (inbreeding, genetic pollution from GMOs), species (overexploitation, IAS), ecosystem (fragmentation, climate change)
Invasive Alien Species (IAS) as a crosscutting threat affecting all three levels — examples: Lantana camara, water hyacinth in India
Climate change as emerging #1 threat by 2050 per IPBES — species range shifts, phenological mismatches

concepts.name: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD): Objectives, Protocols, and India's Obligations
key_dimensions: Three objectives: conservation, sustainable use, fair and equitable sharing of benefits — all three are equally primary (UPSC trap: not just conservation)
Nagoya Protocol (ABS) vs. Cartagena Protocol (Biosafety) — different subjects, both under CBD umbrella — frequently confused in UPSC
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022): 30×30 target — distinction from Paris Agreement targets
India's Biological Diversity Act 2002 and its 2023 amendments — NBA, SBBs, BMCs hierarchy

concepts.name: Biosphere Reserves: Zonation, MAB Programme, and Distinction from Other PAs
key_dimensions: Three-zone model: core (strictly protected), buffer (limited research/tourism), transition/cooperation zone (sustainable use) — functions of each zone
UNESCO Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme — not a legally binding treaty, voluntary nomination (UPSC trap: not under WPA)
India: 18 Biosphere Reserves, 12 under UNESCO's World Network — which ones are NOT in UNESCO network is a frequent UPSC trap
Biosphere reserves as living laboratories — role in conserving all three levels of biodiversity simultaneously

concepts.name: Species-Area Relationship and Its Implications for Habitat Fragmentation
key_dimensions: S = cA^z equation — what z-value indicates for islands vs. continental habitats (z=0.1–0.2 for continental, 0.2–0.35 for islands)
Application to habitat fragmentation: smaller fragments → fewer species → why connectivity matters
SLOSS debate (Single Large Or Several Small reserves) — current consensus and its limitations
India's wildlife corridor policy (e.g., Kaziranga-Karbi Anglong) as applied species-area and metapopulation theory

concepts.name: Megadiverse Countries: Criteria, India's Status, and Policy Implications
key_dimensions: IUCN/UNEP criteria: countries harboring majority of Earth's species — ~17 countries hold 70%+ of biodiversity
India's statistics: 7–8% of global species on 2.4% land area — 4 global biodiversity hotspots within territory
Like Minded Megadiverse Countries (LMMC) group — India's diplomatic role in CBD negotiations, distinct from G20 biodiversity commitments
UPSC trap: megadiverse ≠ hotspot — Amazon Basin countries are megadiverse but may not meet hotspot criteria (intact habitat)

concepts.name: Genetic Diversity Conservation: Seed Banks, Cryopreservation, and Assisted Evolution
key_dimensions: Svalbard Global Seed Vault vs. national gene banks — purpose distinction (backup vs. active collection)
Cryopreservation of animal genetic material — relevance for functionally extinct species (Northern White Rhino case)
Assisted gene flow as a conservation tool under climate change — ethical and ecological risks
India: NBPGR (plant), NBAGR (animal), NBFGR (fish) — three separate bureaus for genetic resource conservation (frequently tested)

concepts.name: Functional Diversity vs. Taxonomic Diversity: Beyond Species Counting
key_dimensions: Functional diversity: variety of ecological roles/traits rather than number of species — why two ecosystems with same species count can differ functionally
Functional redundancy: multiple species performing same role — insurance hypothesis for ecosystem stability
UPSC relevance: explains why protecting 'common' species matters, not just rare ones — counter to charismatic megafauna bias
Phylogenetic diversity as third dimension — evolutionary distinctiveness (EDGE species concept) — why protecting an evolutionarily unique species has outsized conservation value
